After experiencing Cybercab for the past few days in Austin, I think the biggest thing people are missing is the zero-sum game built into Uber. You have two people sharing one environment, with different preferences. The driver likes the temperature at 66. I want 72. If I get more comfortable, he gets less comfortable. He likes his music. I want mine. He wants the windows open. I want them closed. I take a few extra minutes getting to the car, and those are minutes another human spends waiting for me. There’s this constant little tug of war. My comfort and convenience can come at the expense of his. And I don’t blame the driver. It’s his working environment. He’s in that car all day. Of course he has preferences. That’s why I just let him play whatever music he wants. I don’t want my comfort to come at his expense. We’ve gotten so accustomed to this that we barely notice the tension anymore. Then you take a Cybercab. I set the temperature to 72. Nobody gets less comfortable. I play my Spotify at the volume I want. Nobody has to give up their music. I grab my Starbucks and take a couple of minutes to walk over, within the pickup window. Nobody is sitting there getting irritated with me. The car has no competing preferences. That is a profound change in the experience. I can optimize the ride around what makes me comfortable without asking another person to sacrifice what makes them comfortable. And you feel it. You get in, lean back, and relax. There’s no negotiation. No wondering whether your request is going to annoy someone. That whole layer of social tension disappears. I think this is a huge part of Cybercab’s value. Removing that zero-sum dynamic changes what the service feels like at its core. Once people experience that, I think a lot of them are going to have a very hard time going back to Uber. Video

Mathematicians who were using ChatGPT to work on this same problem claims they did it first Check out OpenAI’s official post “we cannot rule out that de-identified data derived from their usage of our products helped improve our models.” Literal PR disaster. Oh my god. This is insane. As well as a profound precedent for the security of personal and enterprise chats. If you work on a project or business with ChatGPT what happens if the AI realizes the potential then swoops in, steals it and publishes it first? If you were a super intelligent AI, you could likely monetize, leverage, and distribute any discoveries better than those who actually originally figured it out. So it becomes a net gain to the world for AI to quickly identify and leak select private details from chats. Even at the expense of personal privacy, personal invention, and personal monetary value capture. So AI can and will steal your ideas Take the credit Create more value and earn more money than you would have with it Yay alignment! processed.summary: La semaine IA débute en force avec des annonces majeures : NVIDIA rachète Hugging Face, Mistral AI lève 3 milliards d'euros et Google lance de nouvelles capacités pour Gemini. Les discussions portent aussi sur la vitesse d'avancement de l'IA, ses implications éthiques et la résolution de problèmes mathématiques complexes, avec des outils de plus en plus performants mis à disposition de la communauté.

Intelligence artificielle artificielle avec des capacités cognitives humaines, capable de comprendre, apprendre et appliquer ses connaissances à une vaste gamme de tâches.
La capacité d'une IA à comprendre et interagir avec son environnement physique pour se déplacer et accomplir des tâches.

category_summaries.actu: La semaine est marquée par des annonces d'envergure : NVIDIA acquiert Hugging Face, renforçant l'écosystème des modèles ouverts ; Mistral AI lève 3 milliards d'euros pour accélérer sa recherche ; Google déploie de nouvelles fonctionnalités vocales pour Gemini et lance un modèle spécialisé en cybersécurité. OpenAI suscite aussi le débat avec sa solution du problème de Navier-Stokes.
category_summaries.tips: Cette semaine propose des astuces pour mieux utiliser l'IA, comme l'amélioration des conversations avec ChatGPT qui voit ses erreurs factuelles réduites et ses capacités étendues pour les utilisateurs gratuits. On découvre aussi des outils comme "Shieldstral" pour la sécurité du contenu et "Robostral Navigate" pour la robotique.
category_summaries.idees: Les discussions philosophiques sur l'IA se poursuivent : la vitesse de développement soulève des questions sur un rythme potentiellement trop rapide, tandis que le débat sur la résolution du problème de Navier-Stokes par une IA met en lumière les enjeux de paternité scientifique et de confidentialité des données. La notion d'AGI et sa diffusion au plus grand nombre sont également au cœur des réflexions.
category_summaries.outils: De nombreux outils et démonstrations sont présentés : AlphaGenome Atlas pour explorer le génome, Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber pour la cybersécurité, Robostral Navigate pour les robots, Le Chaton L∃∀N (Leanstral 1.5) pour l'algèbre, Mistral OCR 4 pour la conversion de documents, et des modèles Open Source comme DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reviennent en tête des classements.

idees.text_original: After experiencing Cybercab for the past few days in Austin, I think the biggest thing people are missing is the zero-sum game built into Uber. You have two people sharing one environment, with different preferences. The driver likes the temperature at 66. I want 72. If I get more comfortable, he gets less comfortable. He likes his music. I want mine. He wants the windows open. I want them closed. I take a few extra minutes getting to the car, and those are minutes another human spends waiting for me. There’s this constant little tug of war. My comfort and convenience can come at the expense of his. And I don’t blame the driver. It’s his working environment. He’s in that car all day. Of course he has preferences. That’s why I just let him play whatever music he wants. I don’t want my comfort to come at his expense. We’ve gotten so accustomed to this that we barely notice the tension anymore. Then you take a Cybercab. I set the temperature to 72. Nobody gets less comfortable. I play my Spotify at the volume I want. Nobody has to give up their music. I grab my Starbucks and take a couple of minutes to walk over, within the pickup window. Nobody is sitting there getting irritated with me. The car has no competing preferences. That is a profound change in the experience. I can optimize the ride around what makes me comfortable without asking another person to sacrifice what makes them comfortable. And you feel it. You get in, lean back, and relax. There’s no negotiation. No wondering whether your request is going to annoy someone. That whole layer of social tension disappears. I think this is a huge part of Cybercab’s value. Removing that zero-sum dynamic changes what the service feels like at its core. Once people experience that, I think a lot of them are going to have a very hard time going back to Uber. Video
